rail_monitor.package: WSON-6 DSE, 1.5 x 1.5 mm, 0.5 mm pitch
rail_monitor.source_buck_feedback_assumptions: LMR51430 VFB 0.591..0.609 V, 100k/22.1k feedback resistors +/-1%, opposing 100 ppm/C TCR over 60 C, and +/-50 nA FB leakage; the source's declared 3.135..3.465 V envelope is retained as the acceptance bound
rail_monitor.ct_configuration: CT left unconnected; TI no-capacitor propagation delay is approximately 25 us minimum. No added release delay is assumed in the assertion budget.
rail_monitor.corner_method: Vtrip=(Vthreshold-Iin*Rth)*(Rtop+Rbottom)/Rbottom; independent +/-0.1% resistor tolerance, opposing +/-25 ppm/C TCR over 60 C, +/-100 nA SENSE current, and 1% threshold accuracy. Rising bound conservatively applies max VITN accuracy and max 0.825% hysteresis.
rail_monitor.verdict: PASS bounded rail guard: falling trip minimum 3.006010 V is above the MAX31865 3.0 V minimum, and rising clear maximum 3.114708 V is below the 3.1332 V minimum valid local RTD_AVDD rail. This closes the deterministic low-valid-rail release corner in the source/model envelope; reset transients, rail ramp, PCB parasitics, and physical loss behavior remain NOT RUN.

high_window_trip_boundary_ohm_estimate.meaning: The independent hardware HIGH comparator can trip before the 300 ohm firmware open threshold. It is guaranteed clear through about 262.7 ohm, corner/offset dependent from about 262.7 to 293.6 ohm, and guaranteed fault by 300 ohm under the declared model. This is intentional coarse-window behavior only if the system accepts the earlier trip.

hardware_window.verdict: PASS for passive REFIN-/ISENSOR window under declared corners; open margin is 9.76 mV after +/-4 mV comparator offset and requires the stated assumptions

superseded_tps3700_result.disposition: Superseded: fail-safe trip but could not guarantee release at 3.1332 V local minimum.

diagnostic_bias.healthy_load_model: Paired network includes 430 ohm RREF/RTD, 1 ohm sense lead/contact resistance, pullup +/-5% and independent +/-14 nA input leakage; worst RTD=194.1 ohm error is 0.1845 mV, about 0.084 ohm or 0.22 C in this passive model
diagnostic_bias.runtime_fault_assumption: A conductor open is present before BIAS startup for the 90 ms startup-open bound; a conditional continuous-conversion model bounds an arbitrary runtime break by 13.9 ms settling overlap plus 55 ms conversion, one 10 ms control poll, and 5 ms sink allocation (83.9 ms), with one possibly contaminated sample. The 13.9 ms term includes worst 1M pullup +100 ppm/C and 1nF C0G +30 ppm/C drift over 60 C, plus +/-5% and <=200 pF parasitic corners.

runtime_filter_evidence.datasheet_facts: MAX31865 specifies a 60 Hz continuous conversion period of 16.7..17.6 ms and says the first conversion after enabling continuous mode takes the single-conversion time of 52..55 ms; it labels the block a 50/60 Hz digital SINC filter but gives no step-response or phase-reset guarantee
runtime_filter_evidence.bounded_model_assumption: For the 83.9 ms conditional bound, three 17.6 ms periods (52.8 ms) are treated as a conservative third-order boxcar history and covered by the 55 ms single-conversion maximum
runtime_filter_evidence.closure_needed: Vendor step-response evidence or an instrumented runtime-break test must confirm filter-history clearing and arbitrary-break detection latency before claiming the 100 ms runtime requirement closed

proposed_protocol_budget_ms.sequence: enable BIAS (0x80), wait 2 ticks, one-time automatic fault (0x84), wait 1 tick, continuous conversion (0xC0), wait falling DRDY, read RTD data first then fault status; leave continuous conversion armed

timing.spi_margin: MAX31865 5 MHz maximum; source uses mode 1 and 500 kHz
timing.critical_gap: The datasheet typical 100 nF RTD filter with a 10 Mohm diagnostic pullup would make tau about 1 s and is rejected. Selected paired 1 Mohm pullups and 1 nF C0G with <=200 pF parasitic give worst temperature-adjusted tau 1.323 ms and 10.5 tau 13.9 ms, so startup-open inputs are settled before continuous conversion launches at 30 ms. RC settling overlaps the mandatory startup/diagnostic phases; it is not added to the MAX 55 ms conversion bound. The 60 Hz MAX conversion bound is treated as the complete ADC/filter observation interval; the runtime timing model assumes the third-order filter history has settled within that bound (three 17.6 ms periods = 52.8 ms, covered by 55 ms), with no extra additive filter delay. The MAX 55 ms conversion maximum completes at or before the next 10 ms control tick (90 ms from startup sequence), leaving 10 ms total; reserve 5 ms for fault-sink/control handoff. A runtime break is observed within 13.9 ms settling overlap + 55 ms conversion + 10 ms poll + 5 ms sink budget (83.9 ms), with one contaminated sample possible. Local REFIN window thresholds do not detect isolated SENSE opens. MAX common-mode/internal-switch behavior, MAX gain/offset, EMC, physical wiring, and complete accuracy remain NOT RUN.
